meta.name: Mixed Overdose — RSI for Refractory Respiratory Depression

history.hpi: Roommate returned home to find the patient unresponsive on the bathroom floor with an uncapped hypodermic needle and an empty alprazolam pill bottle nearby. Patient was last seen normal approximately 45 minutes prior. Roommate reports a history of polysubstance use and recent relapse.
pastMedical: Opioid use disorder, in and out of treatment
medications: Buprenorphine/naloxone (Suboxone) - reportedly not taking as prescribed
history.lastOralIntake: Unknown; roommate last saw him eat dinner approximately 6 hours prior
history.events: Roommate found patient unresponsive on the bathroom floor and called 911 immediately

scene.location: Second-floor apartment bathroom, patient supine on tile floor between the toilet and tub
scene.safety: Uncapped hypodermic needle on the floor near the patient; sharps precautions and gloves required
scene.bystanders: Roommate present, called 911, reports finding the patient like this and provides history of substance use
visualCues: Patient unresponsive, supine on bathroom floor
Empty alprazolam pill bottle and uncapped needle within reach

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew finds a 44-year-old male unresponsive on the bathroom floor with pinpoint pupils, cyanotic lips, and slow, shallow respirations. Drug paraphernalia and an empty pill bottle are visible nearby.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent but at risk; snoring respirations, minimal spontaneous effort
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse present but weak, skin pale and cool
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: No purposeful movement, no response to painful stimulus
otherFindings: Cyanosis of lips and nail beds
Track marks noted on bilateral antecubital areas

transitions.condition: Crew opens and supports the airway with BVM ventilation and oxygen before administering titrated naloxone for suspected opioid overdose.

phases.name: Airway supported, naloxone titrated
phases.description: Crew supports ventilation with BVM and oxygen, then administers titrated naloxone. Mental status and respirations improve only partially, consistent with a mixed overdose (benzodiazepine co-ingestion) rather than pure opioid toxicity.
phases.triggerCondition: Critical resuscitation (airway, oxygen, ventilation support) is performed before naloxone is given, per protocol priority. Naloxone is titrated in incremental doses, but respiratory depression and altered mental status only partially resolve, indicating a mixed-substance overdose that will not fully reverse with naloxone alone.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent with BVM assistance, OPA in place
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Assisted, shallow spontaneous effort at 8/min, still inadequate tidal volume
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse present, skin improving color
otherFindings: Moans to painful stimulus but does not follow commands
Respiratory effort remains inadequate despite naloxone
No signs of opioid withdrawal (no agitation, no vomiting)

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess airway, breathing, circulation, and mental status
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Assess the patient's airway, breathing, circulation, and mental status
expectedActions.rationale: Establishes baseline severity and rules out other causes of altered mental status.

expectedActions.shortAction: Support airway and ventilation with BVM and oxygen before naloxone
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Critical resuscitation (opening and/or maintaining the airway, provision of oxygen, ensuring adequate circulation) should be performed prior to naloxone administration. Support the patient's airway by positioning, oxygen administration, and ventilator assistance with a bag valve mask if necessary
expectedActions.rationale: Ventilation and oxygenation take priority over naloxone administration per protocol sequencing.

expectedActions.shortAction: Naloxone 0.4 mg IV, titrate up to 2 mg IV until adequate respiratory effort
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Adults: The typical initial adult dose ranges between Naloxone 0.4–2 mg IV, IM, up to a dose of 4 mg IN or 5 mg ETT. The administration of naloxone can be titrated until adequate respiratory effort is achieved if administered with a syringe IV, IM, IN, or ETT
expectedActions.rationale: Titrated dosing reverses respiratory depression while minimizing precipitated withdrawal.

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize respiratory depression persists despite naloxone; prepare for RSI
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Regardless of the doses of naloxone administered, airway management with provision of adequate oxygenation and ventilation is the primary goal in patients with confirmed or suspected opioid overdose
expectedActions.rationale: A mixed overdose with a non-opioid sedative on board will not fully reverse with naloxone, so definitive airway management must proceed.

expectedActions.shortAction: Preoxygenate with high-flow O2 and positive pressure ventilation ≥2 minutes before RSI
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patient should be pre-oxygenated with high flow oxygen, and positive pressure ventilation for a minimum of two minutes prior to the procedure
expectedActions.rationale: Adequate preoxygenation extends the safe apnea time during laryngoscopy and reduces peri-intubation hypoxia risk.

transitions.condition: Crew preoxygenates with high-flow oxygen and positive pressure ventilation for a full two minutes prior to attempting RSI.
Crew proceeds directly to sedation and paralysis without completing an adequate preoxygenation period.

phases.name: RSI performed, tube secured
phases.description: After adequate preoxygenation, the crew performs RSI: premedication, induction, paralysis, intubation, and placement confirmation with waveform capnography. The patient is now ventilated with a secured advanced airway.
phases.triggerCondition: Following a full two-minute preoxygenation period, the crew proceeds with rapid sequence intubation per protocol, confirms tube placement with continuous waveform capnography, and secures the tube.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Secured with endotracheal tube, confirmed placement
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Ventilated via BVM at 10-12/min, equal bilateral chest rise
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse strong and regular, skin warming
otherFindings: ETT confirmed with waveform capnography, bilateral breath sounds, no gastric sounds

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 82 mcg IV (82 kg × 1 mcg/kg) 2-3 minutes before intubation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Consider pre-medication with Fentanyl, 1 mcg/kg, 2-3 minutes prior to intubation attempt
expectedActions.rationale: Blunts the sympathetic response to laryngoscopy.

expectedActions.shortAction: Ketamine 123 mg IV push (82 kg × 1.5 mg/kg) for induction sedation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer induction sedative agent: Etomidate IV push, 0.2-0.3 mg/kg OR Ketamine IV push, 1-2 mg/kg OR Midazolam IV push, 0.05-0.10 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Induction sedation must precede paralysis to prevent an awake paralysis.

expectedActions.shortAction: Rocuronium 82 mg IV push (82 kg × 1 mg/kg) for paralysis
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer paralytic agent: Succinylcholine IV push, 1-2 mg/kg OR Rocuronium IV push, 1 mg/kg OR Vecuronium IV push, 0.1 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Paralysis optimizes intubating conditions and first-pass success.

expectedActions.shortAction: Intubate; confirm placement with waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Confirm placement of advanced airway (endotracheal tube, SGA) with waveform capnography (most reliable), absent gastric sounds, and bilateral breath sounds
expectedActions.rationale: Waveform capnography is the most reliable confirmation method and must be checked before trusting placement.

expectedActions.shortAction: Secure tube; ventilate at 10-12 breaths/min, target EtCO2 35-45 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Secure tube manually. Once proper position is confirmed, secure the tube with tape, twill, or commercial device. Adult: 10–12 breaths/minute
expectedActions.rationale: Prevents tube dislodgement and avoids hyperventilation-induced hypotension.

phases.name: RSI attempted without preoxygenation
phases.description: The crew moves directly to sedation and paralysis without completing adequate preoxygenation. During the intubation attempt, the patient desaturates and becomes bradycardic — peri-intubation hypoxia.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew proceeds to sedation and paralysis without a full two-minute preoxygenation period. During the laryngoscopy attempt, SpO2 falls below 90% and heart rate drops, indicating peri-intubation hypoxia and bradycardia.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Open, laryngoscope in place, tube not yet placed
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Apneic — paralyzed, no ventilation occurring during attempt
otherFindings: SpO2 falling rapidly during the attempt

expectedActions.shortAction: Stop attempt at desaturation <90%; resume BVM ventilation with PEEP
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Attempt intubation, limiting attempts to 15 seconds, or a desaturation below 90%, whichever occurs first. Meticulous attention should be paid to avoiding hypoxia and hypotension during intubation attempts to limit patient morbidity and mortality
expectedActions.rationale: Continuing an attempt through desaturation risks hypoxic cardiac arrest.
